shared_elements: carved human figure (frontal colossus in A, profile figures in B)
relief-carved surface detail on a stone monument
curved/spiral forms (disc and scrolls in A, ram horns in B)
justification: Both surfaces carry carved human imagery and low-relief detail, and both include prominent curved/spiral forms (the concentric disc and volutes on A, the ram horns and curled hair in B), but these are generic correspondences. A is a frontal, three-dimensional colossal figure whose body carries isolated emblematic motifs (disc, scrolls, small sign-like elements) with no narrative, whereas B is a flat processional frieze of bearded profile men driving two horned rams — different subjects, different relationships, and different compositional logic.
